REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANGKA REGENCY

NUMBER 9 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF BANGKA,

Considering:

a. that women's empowerment is carried out so that women can actualize their potential optimally to participate in development in accordance with their nature and capacity; b. that women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and preparation of quality generations, need to receive guarantees of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination in order to build society, nation and state; c. that based on the provisions of Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, mandates that women's empowerment is a mandatory affair implemented by the Regency Regional Government; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 28 of 1959 concerning Stipulation of Emergency Law Number 4 of 1956 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1956 Number 55) Emergency Law Number 5 of 1956 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1956 Number 56) and Emergency Law Number 6 of 1956 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1956 Number 57) concerning the Establishment of Level II Regions including Kotaparaja Within the Level I Region of South Sumatra As Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1959 Number 73, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 1821); 3. Law Number 27 of 2000 concerning the Establishment of Bangka Belitung Islands Province (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2002 Number 217, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia 4033); 4. Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1945 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1974 Number 1, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3019); 5. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on The Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 6. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1999 Number 165 Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 7. Law Number 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2003 Number 39, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4279); 8. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 9. Law Number 13 of 2006 concerning Protection of Witnesses and Victims (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2006 Number 64, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4635), as amended by Law Number 31 of 2014 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 293, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5601); 10. Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2007 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4720); 11. Law Number 11 of 2009 concerning Social Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2009 Number 12, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4967); 12. Government Regulation Number 4 of 2006 concerning Implementation and Cooperation for Recovery of Victims of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2006 Number 15, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4604); 16. Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment Number 1 of 2008 concerning Guidelines for Improving the Quality of Life of Women; 18. Article 23

1. The implementation of Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 13 letter j is intended to provide legal protection and/or trauma and health recovery.
2. Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal aid;
b. assistance following the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
d. trauma and health services.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 12

1. Protection of women includes:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
2. Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of a decent living.
3. Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability due to shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
4. Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be implemented in terms of providing protection to women who are witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

Article 4

The purpose of this Regional Regulation is:
a. to empower women both individually and in groups and society at large so that they are able to live more independently; and
b. to prevent and address the risks of violence and vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled according to the principles of equality and justice.

Article 18

1. Implementation of protection for domestic women workers as referred to in Article 13 letter e is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.
2. Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection for:
a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions;
b. health and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE REGENCY REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 6

1. The Regency Regional Government is obligated and responsible for the empowerment and protection of women.
2. The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Part Six

Article 19

1. Implementation of protection for women heads of household as referred to in Article 13 letter f is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women heads of household.
2. Women heads of household as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as economic supporters of the family;
b. strengthening of capacity and recognition as heads of household in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 20

1. The implementation of Protection for women former inmates of Correctional Institutions as referred to in Article 13 letter g is intended to provide protection from obstacles to adjusting to life in society, so that they can carry out life normally.
2. Women former inmates of Correctional Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
b. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 21

1. The implementation of Protection for women victims of disaster as referred to in Article 13 letter h is intended to provide protection during disasters and post-disaster.
2. Women victims of disaster as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. access to decent housing;
b. health services;
c. information access services and legal consultation; and
d. post-disaster recovery.

Article 26

1. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter a is implemented through:
a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of program and activity planning with related Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities is further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
3. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Regency development planning.
4. The budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter b is implemented through general budget policies set forth in the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
5. The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter c is implemented through:
a. implementation of programs and activities set forth in the budget documents of Regional Apparatus; and
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus.
6. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in Article 25 letter d is implemented through:a. conducting periodic monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of programs and activities that have been carried out; and b. making periodic reports.

Article 22

1. The implementation of Protection for women commercial sex workers as referred to in Article 13 letter i is intended to provide health protection and improvement of life skills as capital to improve social status.
2. Protection for women commercial sex workers as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. providing life skills;
b. facilitating reproductive health services; and
c. preventing the occurrence of human trafficking.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 12

1. Protection of women includes:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
2. Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of a decent living.
3. Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability due to shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
4. Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be implemented in terms of providing protection to women who are witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 4

The purpose of this Regional Regulation is:
a. to empower women both individually and in groups and society at large so that they are able to live more independently; and
b. to prevent and address the risks of violence and vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled according to the principles of equality and justice.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

Article 19

1. Implementation of protection for women heads of household as referred to in Article 13 letter f is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women heads of household.
2. Women heads of household as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as economic supporters of the family;
b. strengthening of capacity and recognition as heads of household in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

Article 4

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE REGENCY REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 6

1. The Regency Regional Government is obligated and responsible for the empowerment and protection of women.
2. The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 26

1. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter a is implemented through:
a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of program and activity planning with related Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities is further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
3. The formulation of policy planning for programs and activities for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Regency development planning.
4. The budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter b is implemented through general budget policies set forth in the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
5. The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter c is implemented through:
a. implementation of programs and activities set forth in the budget documents of Regional Apparatus; and
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus.
6. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in Article 25 letter d is implemented through:a. conducting periodic monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of programs and activities that have been carried out; and b. making periodic reports.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 12

1. Protection of women includes:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
2. Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of a decent living.
3. Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability due to shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
4. Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be implemented in terms of providing protection to women who are witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER VI

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Article 23

1. The implementation of Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 13 letter j is intended to provide legal protection and/or trauma and health recovery.
2. Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal aid;
b. assistance following the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
d. trauma and health services.

Part Eleven

Women Victims of Violence

Article 19

1. Implementation of protection for women heads of household as referred to in Article 13 letter f is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women heads of household.
2. Women heads of household as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as economic supporters of the family;
b. strengthening of capacity and recognition as heads of household in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 22

1. The implementation of Protection for women commercial sex workers as referred to in Article 13 letter i is intended to provide health protection and improvement of life skills as capital to improve social status.
2. Protection for women commercial sex workers as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. providing life skills;
b. facilitating reproductive health services; and
c. preventing the occurrence of human trafficking.

Article 18

1. Implementation of protection for domestic women workers as referred to in Article 13 letter e is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.

CHAPTER IX

FINANCING

Article 27

All costs for the implementation of policy planning for programs and activities related to Women's Empowerment and Protection are sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. Other sources that are lawful and non-binding in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 4

a. to empower women both individually and in groups and society at large so that they are able to live more independently; and
b. to prevent and address the risks of violence and vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled according to the principles of equality and justice.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANGKA REGENCY

NUMBER 9 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF BANGKA,

Considering:

a. that women's empowerment is carried out so that women can actualize their potential optimally to participate in development in accordance with their nature and capacity; b. that women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and preparation of quality generations, need to receive guarantees of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination in order to build society, nation and state; c. that based on the provisions of Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, mandates that women's empowerment is a mandatory affair implemented by the Regency Regional Government; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection; In View of:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

Article 15

1. Implementation of protection for elderly women as referred to in Article 13 letter b is in order to extend life expectancy so that they can carry out their social functions and play an active role naturally in their social life.
2. Elderly women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. basic health services to maintain and improve health status including psychological services and diseases related to the elderly (gerontological/geriatric);;
b. use of facilities and accessibility of public facilities and infrastructure; and
c. government administration services.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 11

1. Women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 7 letter d includes:
a. enhancement of awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
2. Women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

Article 24

1. Women's empowerment and protection is implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.
2. In women's empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services are established as determined by Regent's Decree.
3. Women's empowerment and protection is coordinated by the Agency responsible for Women's Empowerment.

Article 21

1. The implementation of Protection for women victims of disaster as referred to in Article 13 letter h is intended to provide protection during disasters and post-disaster.
2. Women victims of disaster as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. access to decent housing;
b. health services;
c. information access services and legal consultation; and
d. post-disaster recovery.

Article 22

1. The implementation of Protection for women commercial sex workers as referred to in Article 13 letter i is intended to provide health protection and improvement of life skills as capital to improve social status.

a. providing life skills;
b. facilitating reproductive health services; and
c. preventing the occurrence of human trafficking.

Article 23

1. The implementation of Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 13 letter j is intended to provide legal protection and/or trauma and health recovery.
2. Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal aid;
b. assistance following the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
d. trauma and health services.

Article 19

1. Implementation of protection for women heads of household as referred to in Article 13 letter f is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women heads of household.
2. Women heads of household as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection rights for:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as economic supporters of the family;
b. strengthening of capacity and recognition as heads of household in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 18

1. Implementation of protection for domestic women workers as referred to in Article 13 letter e is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.
2. Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection for:
a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions;
b. health and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

CHAPTER VII

STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

Article 24

1. Women's empowerment and protection is implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.
2. In women's empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services are established as determined by Regent's Decree.
3. Women's empowerment and protection is coordinated by the Agency responsible for Women's Empowerment.

Article 4

The purpose of this Regional Regulation is:
a. to empower women both individually and in groups and society at large so that they are able to live more independently; and
b. to prevent and address the risks of violence and vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled according to the principles of equality and justice.

Article 21

1. The implementation of Protection for women victims of disaster as referred to in Article 13 letter h is intended to provide protection during disasters and post-disaster.
2. Women victims of disaster as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. access to decent housing;
b. health services;
c. information access services and legal consultation; and
d. post-disaster recovery.

CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE REGENCY REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 6

1. The Regency Regional Government is obligated and responsible for the empowerment and protection of women.
2. The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.

Article 11

a. enhancement of awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.

c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 24

a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

b. health and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 12

1. Protection of women includes:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
2. Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of a decent living.
3. Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability due to shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
4. Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be implemented in terms of providing protection to women who are witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

Article 20

1. The implementation of Protection for women former inmates of Correctional Institutions as referred to in Article 13 letter g is intended to provide protection from obstacles to adjusting to life in society, so that they can carry out life normally.
2. Women former inmates of Correctional Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
b. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of doing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to do household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.
